h: Kiddush Draws the Blessing of Torah Into Shabbos

p: זָכוֹר אֶת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת לְקַדְּשׁוֹ (שְׁמוֹת כ, ח)
"Remember the day of Shabbos to sanctify it" (Shemos 20:8):
that is, through the sanctification of the day
that we recite over the mitzvah of Shabbos,
and took pleasure in us," etc.,
And in the holy Zohar at the beginning of this parashah:
וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ וּבֵרַכְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר (דְּבָרִים ח, י)
"'And you will eat and be satisfied, and bless,' etc. (Devarim 8:10):
for all that one eats and drinks
and benefits from in this world;
and if he does not bless,
'One who robs his father and his mother,'" etc.
So too it is found in the Gemara (Berachos 35b)
who instituted the text of the blessings.
Afterward it is found in the holy Zohar:
"to know the secret of the blessings
over the commandments of the Torah
and over all the pleasures and delights
which is also learned from this pasuk
"When he is satisfied he blesses," etc.;
And what it says, "over the commandments of the Torah,"
refers to the blessing over the Torah
and the blessing over the mitzvos,
from this pasuk by kal vachomer,
עַל הָאָרֶץ הַטּוֹבָה אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לָךְ
"for the good land that He gave you,"
"And I will give you the Tablets of stone"
דִּבְרִיךְ בַּר נָשׁ לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
with which a person blesses HaKadosh Baruch Hu
לִשְׁמֵיהּ דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא קַדִּישָׁא וְכוּלֵּי
to the Name of HaKadosh Baruch Hu the holy," etc.,
"and they come to draw from there
"From what place do they come down?
from the place of the head of the Tzaddik," etc.,
'Blessings upon the head of the righteous';
it pours out to this bride," etc.
וּבְשַׁבָּת אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פח, א)
And regarding Shabbos it is found in the holy Zohar (II 88a):
the head of Zeir Anpin is filled
with the dew that descends from Atika Kadisha,
and it casts it to the Field of Apples."
a time of flow in Torah she'b'al peh,
which is from the dew of Atika
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן יט, לח, ב)
And through the blessings of the mitzvah of Shabbos,
which is the sanctification of the day,
"and it casts it to the Field of Apples";
and that is why it says,
"Remember the day of Shabbos to sanctify it."
And it is found in the Rekanati
that Eretz Yisrael is praised with this
for there are many cities outside the land
And although in the Gemara it appears
that the praise of Eretz Yisrael is in its plain sense,
in all the land of Egypt than Tzoan,
and there is no rockier place
the words of the Rekanati are also true,
are a chariot for the seven middos,
Chitah has the numerical value of twenty-two,
corresponding to the twenty-two letters of the Torah;
corresponds to the aspect of Aharon HaKohen,
the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
"For the lips of the kohen guard knowledge,
and Torah they seek from his mouth";
that comes to rectify the "much anger":
that is, it is effective in rectifying
that wheat includes spelt as well,
and there are in all ten species,
are inferior to barley and wheat,
they allude to the first three,
since the apprehension of the first three
is also a kind of barley,
and it combines with barley as well,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (חַלָּה פֶּרֶק ד מִשְׁנָה ב)
corresponds to the aspect of Kesser Elyon;
וְלָכֵן הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִין חִטִּין
therefore it is also a kind of wheat,
which alludes to Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom:
that is, this is the apprehension
that was included in the Written Torah
is from the dew of Atika,
and as it will be in the future,
they would have been given only
the five Chumashim of the Torah," etc.;
and each one would have apprehended
And so will they apprehend in the future,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
that is, through Torah she'b'al peh
which is the inwardness from Kesser Elyon;
and this is the primordial light
hidden away for those who toil in Torah she'b'al peh
and this is the crownlet of the yud,
and knowledge is pleasant to your soul":
into the depth of the heart,
the aspect of "Binah is the heart,"
which alludes to Torah she'b'al peh,
which correspond to the first three.
"A land in which not in poverty
you will not lack anything in it";
הוּא עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם
is through the middah of Tzaddik Yesod Olam,
כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ עַל (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, יא)
"for all that is in the heavens and on the earth" (Divrei HaYamim I 29:11):
"which holds fast to the heavens and the earth";
and "on the earth," which is called Knesses Yisrael
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א לא, א)
the aspect of the Written Torah:
תּוֹרָה אִיקְרֵי (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב ס, א)
פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינָן לָהּ
"the mouth; we call it Torah she'b'al peh."
"A land whose stones are iron," etc.:
that it is impossible to say
that this was said in praise of Eretz Yisrael,
that it refers to the words of Torah,
and talmidei chachamim are called builders
and this refers to Torah she'b'al peh.
"And you will eat and be satisfied, and bless," etc.,
דְּקָאֵי עַל בִּרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה גַּם כֵּן
which refers to the blessing over the Torah as well,
which is derived by kal vachomer
a time of flow in Torah she'b'al peh,
and so then is the flow
from the Written Torah to the Torah she'b'al peh,
And that is why we bless
in the sanctification of the day:
for it is the flow to the three Avos
from Atika, from the supernal Source,
and from there to the Field of Apples,

— “Rabbi Abba said to Rav Ashi: You learned the proof for this idea from that verse there; we learned it from here, as it is written: “A land whose stones [avaneha] are iron” (Deuteronomy 8:9). Do not read this phrase …”
